title: Patio Screen Enclosures — Juno Beach
h1: Patio Screen Enclosures in Juno Beach, FL
heroParagraph: Enclose your Juno Beach lanai or patio with a custom aluminum screen room built for salt air and coastal winds. Bug-free, shaded outdoor living from Juno Isles to the oceanfront — engineered, permitted, and installed by our in-house crew.
heroImageAlt: Custom aluminum patio screen enclosure on an oceanfront home in Juno Beach, FL with powder-coated frame and panoramic screen walls
introHeading: Screened-In Living Built for Juno Beach's Coastline
valueParagraphs: A screened enclosure turns your Juno Beach lanai, patio, or under-truss porch into living space you'll actually use — free of the mosquitoes and no-see-ums that drift in off the Intracoastal and the dune scrub once the sun drops. We build true screen rooms and Florida-room configurations, framed in powder-coated aluminum, so you get shade, airflow, and a bug-free, pollen-free view of the water or the yard, with leaves and debris kept out, without losing the openness of outdoor living.

Juno Beach sits right on the Atlantic, and from the Intracoastal homes of Juno Isles to the condo corridor along A1A near the pier, every structure here takes the same salt-laden air. Palm Beach County treats this coastline as a Wind-Borne Debris Region, with design winds near 165–175 mph, so a permanent aluminum enclosure needs a permit, sealed engineering, and Florida Product Approval through the town or County PZB. We build to Miami-Dade HVHZ standards — the strictest code in the state — well beyond what's required here.

AB Aluminum & Screens has built more than 500 enclosures across Palm Beach County in 15-plus years, and our in-house crew handles the Juno Beach permit so you're not chasing paperwork. Beyond bug control, a screened room adds privacy from neighboring lanais, keeps pets contained without a leash, and — since Juno Beach restricts beachfront lighting during sea turtle nesting season near Loggerhead Marinelife Center — gives you a shaded space to enjoy evenings outdoors within the town's rules. Every project starts with a free 3D design, and financing is available.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for a screen enclosure in Juno Beach?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any permanent aluminum screen enclosure requires a permit with sealed engineering and Florida Product Approval, reviewed by the Town of Juno Beach or Palm Beach County PZB depending on the project. We handle the entire permit process, so you never have to deal with the county directly.

faqs.question: Are these enclosures rated for hurricanes near the coast?
faqs.answer: Palm Beach County designates this stretch a Wind-Borne Debris Region with design winds near 165–175 mph. We engineer and build every Juno Beach enclosure to Miami-Dade HVHZ product standards, the strictest wind code in Florida, so it exceeds what's actually required here.

faqs.question: What screen options do I have for a Juno Beach enclosure?
faqs.answer: We offer standard fiberglass insect screen, heavier pet- and storm-resistant mesh, and solar/privacy screening that cuts glare and UV off the water. Given the salt air this close to the Atlantic, we also recommend our marine-grade powder-coated frames regardless of which mesh you choose.

faqs.question: Can you enclose my existing covered patio or lanai, and could I convert it to a Florida room later?
faqs.answer: Yes — most Juno Beach projects start with an existing covered patio, lanai, or under-truss area that we frame in and screen. Many owners start with a screen enclosure and later upgrade sections to acrylic or glass panels for a true Florida room, and we can design for that from day one.
